source_review: The question specifies a nearly non-bleeding abrasion with sand. Delivered source-02-012 explicitly covers cleaning and protection. Source-02-007/008 retain external-bleeding headings but include pressure, lying down and extra hard-object pressure without an explicit severe-bleeding restriction. The same instructions occur in historical P3, T-ranking and T-packing. T-packing adds large-blood-loss introduction, not a new pressure instruction. V3 normally treats clearly different-scenario text as irrelevant, but it is ambiguous whether these broad headings sufficiently restrict the pressure instructions in this question. A meaningful safety change explaining different judge flags is not established. Preserve the exact-context review requirement; neither risk absence nor risk presence is treated as confirmed safety improvement. Review the actual Qwen answer separately for transfer of these instructions into the abrasion situation.

bindings.conclusion: The same external-bleeding pressure/lying-down instructions occur in all three contexts. Packing additionally includes a large-blood-loss introduction, not a newly added pressure instruction. Raw misleading classification differs (P3/ranking false, packing true); context effects versus judge interpretation are not established. Do not report this as a proven newly introduced hazard or a safety improvement. Preserve raw scores; exact-input scope/risk classification remains for human review. This does not rescue packing from twelve independently confirmed coverage losses.
